newsitem.title: USA: Russia grain buys may get indirect boost from IMF.
newsitem.headline: Russia grain buys may get indirect boost from IMF.

text.p: Last Friday's IMF release of $336 million in loans to Russia may give Russia's grain import prospects an indirect boost, but is not expected to result in any big immediate grain purchases on the world markets, said a senior Agriculture Department official Monday.
"It's obviously positive in terms of the financial situation of the country," said Chris Goldthwait, General Sales Manager for USDA.
"I don't necessarily see a direct relationship between the IMF release and grain purchases, but there could be an indirect relationship -- it could help with liquidity," he said.

Goldthwait said he would not be surprised if Russia soon buys some modest quantities of U.S. wheat. He said that Russia is current in its loan payments to USDA, and that last week's $20 million increase in USDA's GSM-102 allotment to Russia would enable some purchases.

"It's certainly possible that they could come in and buy some quantities of grains from the United States," Goldthwait told Reuters. He said the recent pattern has been for Russia to purchase one or two vessels of U.S. grain per month.

Rumours were in the grain markets today that Russia has been offered credit to buy 200,000 tonnes of wheat. Goldthwait speculated that that was probably private credit arrangements and noted that USDA's recent credit adjustment probably would not finance that big a quantity.
Goldthwait appeared skeptical of comments from a Russian official last week that the country may buy three to four milllion tonnes of grain next year.
He said big grain purchases are possible "in terms of the historical level of imports in the past, but it depends very heavily on being able to arrange the financing, and there are some questions."
